summary: Clean on the COR dimension. The combine/load/low-level work helpers are correct: make_sheaf_dict dispatches single Node/str/Work vs. collection correctly via the union isinstance, the generated single-row array-load code (combine_utils) and the row-indexed dict-load code (loader_utils) match their callers' usage (load_dict_into_array collects one combined row into a shape-(1,) array; load_array_row_into_dict reads an arbitrary row), ll_make_work initializes inputs/derived/node correctly via determine_field_index over the same _fields list used to build the type (and the zero-source path correctly stores nothing into the empty UniTuple), _verify_signature compares the derive signature against the data/sources-implied signature accurately, the data_ty_ref override path is type-coherent (the returned signature's data arg is the overridden instance type so numba coerces the argument before codegen), and make_work_helper builds the derive signature from typeof(source.data) consistently. No silent-wrong-result, edge-case, or invariant-break defect found. Minor non-COR observations (a duplicated generated-function/overload name 'ol_load_array_row_into_dict' across combine_utils and loader_utils, and an unused enumerate index 'field_ind' in _make_load_to_array_code / _make_load_to_dict_code) are DES/style, out of scope here.
